prs.title: Url encoded token response
prs.author: sebastian-velten
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuth token endpoints on some servers return responses as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` instead of `application/json`, causing the client to fail to parse the token. PR #1531 takes the preventive approach (add `Accept: application/json` to request headers for both exchange and refresh token calls), while PR #1511 takes the defensive approach (parse the `Content-Type` of the response and handle URL-encoded bodies via `parse_qs`). Both changes are in `_exchange_token`/`_handle_token_response` in `src/mcp/client/auth.py` and address the same interoperability gap with non-conforming OAuth servers. (2 PRs)

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuth token endpoints on some servers return responses as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` instead of `application/json`, causing the client to fail to parse the token. PR #1531 takes the preventive approach (add `Accept: application/json` to request headers for both exchange and refresh token calls), while PR #1511 takes the defensive approach (parse the `Content-Type` of the response and handle URL-encoded bodies via `parse_qs`). members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuth token endpoints on some servers return responses as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` instead of `application/json`, causing the client to fail to parse the token. PR #1531 takes the preventive approach (add `Accept: application/json` to request headers for both exchange and refresh token calls), while PR #1511 takes the defensive approach (parse the `Content-Type` of the response and handle URL-encoded bodies via `parse_qs`). Both changes are in `_exchange_token`/`_handle_token_response` in `src/mcp/client/auth.py` and address the same interoperability gap with non-conforming OAuth servers. (2 PRs)
